payload.description: Find code that mints a lifecycle, owner, heartbeat, generation, or session token, then later accepts or rejects asynchronous work by token equality.
positive_signal: token is captured before async work starts
result, heartbeat, cleanup, ownership, or retry decision later compares token equality/inequality
the token minting site has lower entropy or weaker lifecycle scope than the boundary it is supposed to separate
required_gates: G1 token-gated decision: equality/inequality controls accept, reject, pause, retry, cleanup, or ownership
G2 lifecycle overlap: old async work or old owner/session/task can overlap the new lifecycle
G3 collision schedule: two distinct lifecycles can share the same token value under product timing, not only under artificial unit input
G4 strong oracle: a stale result/action is accepted, or an active task/result is rejected, with observable state/action evidence
negative_screens: plain telemetry timestamps, random seeds, last-used metrics, and display-only times
time tokens whose normal renewal interval is larger than token precision and no accelerated product schedule exists
token equality that is only a best-effort log hint and does not gate a state transition

provenance.source: derived from issue51846 owner epoch RED/GREEN and BR registry heartbeat source-screen

name: Identity token distinguishes async lifecycle before accepting result

payload.contract: If a token equality check is used to accept or reject asynchronous work across a lifecycle boundary, distinct lifecycles that can overlap must not share the same token value.
minimal_observation: move to lifecycle B while work/result from A can still arrive
RED if A's token equals B's token and the equality check would accept stale A work as B
GREEN if lifecycle B is forced to mint a distinct token or the stale work is rejected by an additional identity dimension

root_positive.evidence: ownerTS second-granularity collision accepts previous-owner reorg result

payload.screening_rule: Do not execute a candidate until G3 collision schedule is proven from product timing or controllable fault injection.

provenance.source: generalized from DDL owner epoch RED/GREEN

payload.scenario: An asynchronous worker, watcher, heartbeat, or result channel remains live while the owner/session/task/store lifecycle advances to a new epoch.
examples: DDL reorg worker result arrives after owner retire/re-become
restore registry stale checker observes heartbeats while deciding whether a running task is stale
store watcher compares previous and current store start identity
payload.observer_need: the oracle must observe the state transition gated by token equality, not merely that the token values can be equal in a synthetic model

name: Rapid lifecycle renewal versus token precision

payload.schedule: Force two lifecycle epochs close enough that the token minting source may collide, then deliver old async work after the new epoch is active.
required_capability: hold or delay old async result
invalid_if: the product renewal interval is strictly larger than token precision and cannot be accelerated on the relevant path
no observer can distinguish stale work acceptance from a legitimate current result

name: BR restore registry heartbeat and stale-task handling

state_model: mysql.tidb_restore_registry tracks restore tasks and stores status plus last_heartbeat_time as TIMESTAMP(6)
resolveRestoreTS reads CAST(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(last_heartbeat_time) AS UNSIGNED INTEGER) as initialHeartbeatTimestamp
isTaskStale waits up to StaleTaskThresholdMinutes and treats the task as active if heartbeat timestamp changes
transitionStaleTaskToPaused updates status to paused only when last_heartbeat_time equals the expected timestamp
payload.screen_result: matches G1 token-gated decision but fails G3 under default product schedule because heartbeat and stale-check intervals are 60 seconds while token precision is one second

provenance.source: current source inspection after identity-token selector extraction

name: BR registry heartbeat token must distinguish active task from stale task

payload.p_check: isTaskStale and transitionStaleTaskToPaused use last_heartbeat_time equality as the proof that a running/resetting restore task has not made progress.
payload.q_claim: if the heartbeat timestamp did not change over the stale-check window, the task is stale and can be transitioned to paused.
payload.screened_fault: heartbeat updates within the same Unix second would preserve the token and could be mistaken as no heartbeat progress.
payload.why_not_executed: defaultHeartbeatIntervalSeconds is 60 and isTaskStale checks every minute for 5 minutes; under the default product schedule, active heartbeats should advance the one-second token before stale classification. No current product path was found that makes the heartbeat renewal interval smaller than token precision.
source_anchors: br/pkg/registry/heartbeat.go UpdateHeartbeat uses time.Now().UTC().Unix and FROM_UNIXTIME
br/pkg/registry/registration.go selectTaskHeartbeatSQLTemplate casts UNIX_TIMESTAMP(last_heartbeat_time) to integer
payload.method_lesson: A source target must prove G3 collision schedule before execution. Token precision alone is not enough.

name: BR registry same-second heartbeat token collision

payload.fault: Force heartbeat updates to occur within the same Unix second while stale checker observes heartbeat equality.
payload.required_but_missing: a product-supported heartbeat interval or failpoint schedule that can make the heartbeat token collide across the full stale-check window without being purely synthetic
payload.screen_result: INVALID(schedule-proof); default heartbeat and stale checker cadence are one minute

rationale: the DDL owner epoch RED is the seed positive for the identity-token async filter selector
the ownerTS oracle is a concrete instance of lifecycle token uniqueness
BR registry heartbeat matched the token-equality shape but was screened out by missing collision schedule
the same oracle would apply if a product schedule could make heartbeat tokens collide
restore task liveness is observed asynchronously through heartbeats
the candidate failed because the required rapid renewal schedule is not proven under default cadence
the hypothetical fault would need same-second heartbeat updates throughout stale checking
